hints.text: Work from the inside out: first find $\sin 150^\circ$.
$\sin 150^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$. Now ask what $\arcsin\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ is, remembering the range is $[-90^\circ, 90^\circ]$.
$\arcsin\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 30^\circ$, and $150^\circ$ is not allowed as an output.

explanation: Inside first: $\sin 150^\circ = \frac{1}{2}$, because $150^\circ$ has reference angle $30^\circ$ and sine is positive in quadrant II.
Now $\arcsin\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ must return an angle between $-90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$.
The only such angle is $30^\circ$, so the answer is $30^\circ$, not $150^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Inverses only undo on the restricted piece
steps: It is tempting to say the functions cancel and leave $150^\circ$.
They only cancel when the starting angle is already inside the restricted domain $[-90^\circ, 90^\circ]$.
$150^\circ$ is outside it, so $\arcsin$ sends you back to the partner angle that IS inside: $30^\circ$.
